column1: # S3.E "not a second vendor" — must-match / must-not-match case table.
# MATCH means "this model id is the PRIMARY reviewer's own family, so S3.E is void".
# NO-MATCH means "this is a genuinely different vendor and family".
# THE UNIVERSE IS NOT INVENTED. Every id `agy models` printed on 2026-08-31 is here -
# the UNION of two runs hours apart, because the catalogue MOVED between them: the three
# gemini-3.5-flash-* ids were in the first and gone from the second. They stay in the
# table. An id that has left the vendor's catalogue is still an id a stale script can
# pass, and dropping it would shrink this table every time the vendor prunes theirs.
# Beside them are the spellings a harness might use for the same models without the
# vendor prefix. Building a case table from the PATTERN rather than
# from the corpus is F5, and F5 was found the hard way: sixteen real subjects, three
# must-match misses, on a table whose subjects had been written from the regex's own
# vocabulary. So the corpus here is a command's output, pasted.
# The asymmetry that sets the width: a false positive costs a reviewer one edit to the
# model id. A false negative silently voids the arm's whole justification — the receipt
# still reads `antigravity` everywhere a reader looks — and nothing in the artifact says
# so. This is the one rule here whose failure is invisible, so it errs wide.
